host_timing_note: Measured on the FreeRTOS POSIX port, where every task is a thread of a Linux process. Times, jitter and latencies are those of the host's scheduler and are not what the same code shows on a microcontroller. The contents, orderings and sizes of protocol data, and the frames and bytes an exchange takes, do not depend on the host. What happens in a stretch of time does: the jobs and frames of a run of fixed length, ticks dropped, jobs released early; and a stall of the host past the node's 500 ms watchdog or a 1 s protocol timer fails what the node would have passed. Such a failure is never hidden (the bench counts and keeps it, or writes no result), and no stall makes a check pass, so a count of 0 failures holds whatever the host did. An update's time is set by the node's diagnostic task (2 events per 1 ms tick: about 79 ms for each block of 1024 bytes, bench/isotp_throughput.py), the modelled flash (45 ms per sector erase, 0.4 ms per page, each wait ending at a tick) and, after the ECUReset, the flasher's poll for the trial (wait_for_trial: its first request 50 ms after the reset's answer, the next 50 ms after each one that did not find it); the restart itself, fcn_boot as a host process and the trial's start-up, is reset_to_trial, by the node's own log stamps. The host adds its scheduling to each and the tester's Python start-up and turnaround, which a tester on a CAN adapter does not have. The bytes, blocks, steps and slots of an update do not depend on the host's timing; its success can, in one direction only: a stall of the host past the node's 500 ms watchdog or the 1 s ISO-TP timeout fails an update, and none makes one succeed. A failed update is kept with its record and counted, so the updates counted as succeeded did succeed, whatever the host did.

config.order: socketcan then udp, each from a factory flash; the updates of a campaign one after the other, each from the image the one before confirmed
config.node_image: the release node (<build root>/release/bin/fcn_node), stripped (strip -o), packed with fcn_tools.image
config.trial_window: the product's (5 s of good health): no --confirm-periods

big_image.node: started directly with --flash-file (no bootloader), one fresh flash per download; booted through fcn_boot once afterwards if the payload is the node

reset_to_trial.measured: host timing, by the node's own log stamps (CLOCK_MONOTONIC of the host): the download run's 'ECUReset: resetting' line to the trial run's 'started by the bootloader' line; the old run's end, the Board starting fcn_boot again, fcn_boot as a host process (memfd and exec, not a jump) and the trial's start-up
